summary: Monthly team meeting run by Chris Klevan, opening with wins, then setting June projections unit by unit for each rep, then splitting into call reviews. Kim Forbes-Sobers goes into a breakout room to review Kyla Louie's triage calls while Chris reviews two of Ben Byrne's calls with Ben and Andrew Musial - the Sean Stover call from 30 May and the Vibhor Mishra call from 29 May, both of which are separately in this corpus. The coaching centres on opening energy, cutting the 'ready to jump in' transition, getting to the why-now as fast as possible, and fact-checking prospects' self-reported diets rather than accepting them. Chris then reports the results of an AI analysis he ran over every sales call taken in May to identify which prospect types actually close.
notable: Chris Klevan reports an AI analysis of every May sales call and concludes the best-converting prospects are the opposite of the stated ICP: 'the types of people that we found are closing the most often are guys who have the biggest gap. Go figure. They were guys that literally had an injury. They have, like, tons of weight to lose. They've fallen off.'

He names the worst-converting segment as precisely the group the stated ICP describes: 'the guys that just don't really close that often... are the guys who are like, I'm an eight out of 10 or seven out of 10. And I want to get to a 10 out of 10.'
He describes a second high-converting profile: successful on paper 'but they have probably 20 to 25 pounds that they still need to lose', plus former athletes who let their bodies go.
Stated intent to shift lead flow accordingly: 'we are going to try and optimize towards getting more of like the other two tiers. On the calendar versus the guys that are just already shredded'.
Primal University is confirmed as the standing downsell for low-gap prospects: 'You're like, dude, like. Honestly, probably Primal University.'

June projections were set in 'units' and 'sets' per rep per week - Andrew at 13 units for roughly $50k, Ben at 3/4/5/4/2 - with cash collected forecast at 'like 60% upfront cash collected', implying instalments are the norm rather than the exception.

Andrew Musial reports a $100 deposit taken from a prospect that is now being reimbursed: 'the budget is out of his option, but we can discuss this further during our call later today, as well as the reimbursement of the $100 deposit'.
Ben Byrne states he is double-booked for prospect calls: 'I'm double-booked here, so if both guys show up, I'll shoot you texts.'
The internal meeting opens with an explicit recording disclosure - 'meeting is being recorded' - which does not appear on any of the seven sales calls in this batch.
Kim Forbes-Sobers is confirmed as staff and appears as a setter/reviewer, corroborating the KFS title suffix; Kyla Louie is confirmed as the KL suffix and is described as running triages.
Training lineage is named repeatedly - Eli Wilde's surface/action/identity levels and Cole Gordon's teams - as the standard being coached to.
Ben Byrne references having previously sold 'the dating offer', and discloses he is doing a 72-hour fast including a 24-hour dry fast, following a post by Trevor.

Chris coaches reps to distrust self-reported health data: 'you're going to find that people are bullshitters, like crazy. Not because they're genuinely trying to get over on you, but because they actually just overestimate how in shape they are.'

Chris coaches assembling full discovery data so a prospect cannot decline: 'I can build it all out for him, so it seems like the perfect plan that's going to be totally fit to him, and he's going to have, like, no excuses as to why he can't follow it, because we know all the data.'
